advances: Ordinary compact convex bodies and equality of actual cap sets and of the Minkowski midpoint.
author: PK-research-agent
proof: Let $D=(A+B)/2$. For each $i$ the Minkowski midpoint of the endpoint caps lies in $D\cap H_i\subseteq K\cap H_i$ by convexity. Brunn–Minkowski on the positive endpoint caps and the assumed equality give the same positive volume to the two ends of this inclusion chain. A proper compact convex subset of a full-dimensional compact convex body has strictly smaller volume. Indeed, separate an outside point from the closed subset and move it a small distance toward an interior point of the larger body, then take a small interior ball still beyond the separating plane. Thus all three cap sets coincide. Their union gives $K\subseteq D$ and the original containment gives equality. For through-point halfspaces with a positive dependence, the margins cannot all be strictly negative because their positively weighted sum is zero. This proves the cover assertion.
statement:
Let $A,B,K$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let finitely many closed halfspaces $H_i$ cover $K$, with both endpoint caps of positive $d$-volume for every $i$. If
$$
|K\cap H_i|^{1/d}=\frac{|A\cap H_i|^{1/d}+|B\cap H_i|^{1/d}}{2}
$$
for every $i$, then $K=(A+B)/2$ and $K\cap H_i=((A\cap H_i)+(B\cap H_i))/2$ for every $i$. Halfspaces through a common point whose normals admit a positive dependence supply such a cover.
title: An equality cap cover identifies the actual Minkowski midpoint
